content:
incident-bot: [PAGER] service:embeddings-eu latency spike detected in eu-west-1 — auto-page on-call
natalie: on it. seeing increased p50/p95 across all embeddings hosts in eu-west. routing errors also climbing.
sam: confirmed — spans show repeated TCP resets to cloud-egress during KV fetches.
nana (cloud-vendor-liaison): looping in cloud NOC contact (ticket #CN-92418). asking for network fabric check and recent maintenance windows.
natalie: thanks. initial mitigation: scaling down to smaller batch sizes and enabling per-request cold-path fallback. doing canary for 2 nodes now.
lia: support: prepare customer impact list. which customers on dedicated capacity in eu-west? need a targeted outbound if SLA impacted.
sam: quick mitigation commands I ran:
```bash
# reduce embedding batch size
redwoodctl config set embeddings.batch_size 8 --region eu-west-1
# enable kv-cache bypass for requests over 1s
redwoodctl route update --region eu-west-1 --kv-bypass-threshold 1s
```
natalie: results: p50 dropped ~30% on the two canary nodes, errors still present but lower. will keep monitoring.
product-oncall: drafting status page update. suggestion below — please edit: 
"We are investigating increased latency and errors for embeddings in eu-west-1 affecting model endpoints. Some requests may experience degraded performance or timeouts. Our engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 30 minutes."
support-lead: we should prepare a customer notification template for dedicated customers and a simpler note for hosted API customers. I'll draft.
nana (cloud-vendor-liaison): cloud NOC responded: "observed transient packet loss on 10G fabric in eu-west-1 between racks A-B. mitigations in progress; engineering-led ticket open." asked them to escalate to Tier 3.
sam: requesting network trace logs from affected hosts. attaching trace snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] conn reset from 10.0.12.45 -> 10.0.22.7 seq 0x..
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] retransmit count spikes
```
lia: support: here's the customer-impact check I ran:
- 14 dedicated customers with endpoints in eu-west-1
- 220 hosted tenants with >1 request/minute to embeddings in eu-west-1
- 3 customers on active canary who saw timeouts > 5s
I recommend targeted emails to the 14 dedicated customers and a status page public message for hosted.
product-oncall: status update (verbatim) ready for publish after we confirm no false positives: 
"We are currently investigating increased latency and intermittent errors for embeddings in the eu-west-1 region. Some customers may experience slower responses or request timeouts. Our engineers and the cloud provider are actively working on mitigation. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Affected customers on Dedicated plans will receive targeted communication."
support-lead: customer email draft for Dedicated customers: 
"Hi — heads up: we're investigating intermittent latency and timeouts for embedding endpoints in eu-west-1 that may impact your service. We’re actively mitigating (reducing batch sizes, routing adjustments) and working with our cloud provider. Estimated next update: 30 minutes. If you see critical impact please reply and we’ll escalate to a dedicated support engineer. — Redwood Support"
natalie: vendor ask: can cloud NOC confirm scope (fabric vs upstream provider) and ETA for full routing stabilization? also request packet captures and any planned maintenance that could have contributed.
nana (cloud-vendor-liaison): sent a targeted escalation to Tier 3 with packet captures attached, asked for continuous updates and an engineer join on the call. they acknowledged and provided an internal reference: CN-92418-T3.
sam: note for runbook: if vendor indicates fabric-level packet loss and ETA > 30m, switch eu-west traffic to fallback region (eu-central) via smart routing policy and notify customers of temporary region failover.
lia: can we get a quick checklist for SRE to run during handoff? I'll be taking next shift.
natalie: handoff checklist (brief):
- confirm current p50/p95 and error rates
- confirm cloud NOC contact and ticket ID
- confirm mitigation knobs enabled (batch_size, kv-bypass)
- run regional failover dry-run if ETA > 30m
- update status page and notify Dedicated customers
- log all operator commands to incident channel for postmortem
I'll be on-call for 15 more minutes then handing off to lia.
lia: taking it. I'm on the vendor call in 5 mins. pls put any live updates in this thread.
product-oncall: published status page update at 09:35 UTC: "Investigating increased latency and intermittent errors for embeddings in eu-west-1. Active mitigations in progress." link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/embeddings-eu-2026-03-15
support-lead: outbound to Dedicated customers sent at 09:40 UTC. template included CN-92418 ref.
natalie: quick note: we should include an internal one‑pager template for execs if the incident crosses 2 hours — summary of impact, customer list, mitigations, vendor timeline. adding to postmortem backlog.
nana (cloud-vendor-liaison): cloud NOC updated: fabric repair completed at 09:48 UTC, packet loss dropped, final verification in progress. asked us to confirm observed telemetry stable for 15 minutes.
sam: observed p95 back to normal on canary nodes at ~09:52 UTC. full cluster showing gradual recovery by 09:56 UTC.
lia: final checklist before close: confirm vendor close note, confirm no pending customer escalations, create incident timeline, schedule postmortem.
product-oncall: status page update published: "Service restored for embeddings in eu-west-1. Some customers may have seen degraded performance between 09:10–09:50 UTC. If you continue to see issues, contact support."
support-lead: follow-up sent to Dedicated customers with root cause statement and link to postmortem once available.
incident-bot: incident closed — auto-log saved to #incidents and postmortem ticket created: PM-6783.
lia: thanks team. I'll own the postmortem draft and vendor communications summary. please add any missing logs or RKOs to the incident ticket.
